meta.title: Who originally recorded "Papa Was a Rollin' Stone"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Not The Temptations. The Undisputed Truth cut it first, released 9 May 1972 on Gordy; Whitfield re-recorded it with The Temptations that September.
meta.ogTitle: Who originally recorded 'Papa Was a Rollin' Stone'?
meta.ogDescription: The Temptations' No. 1 came second. The Undisputed Truth's Gordy single of 9 May 1972 was the first recording, produced by the same man.

answer.label: Not a Temptations original — a 1972 Undisputed Truth single on Gordy
answer.originalArtistDates: Formed 1970 in Detroit · American psychedelic soul group assembled by Norman Whitfield
answer.sourceLine: The nine-minute Temptations record is so total a piece of work that it is almost always taken for the song’s beginning. It isn’t. Norman Whitfield gave “Papa Was a Rollin’ Stone” first to The Undisputed Truth, whose single came out on Gordy on 9 May 1972 and stalled at No. 63 on the pop chart. Whitfield and Barrett Strong wrote it; Whitfield produced both versions. He then re-cut it with The Temptations, released 28 September 1972 on the same label, and that one went to No. 1 and won three Grammys.

original.heading: Who recorded it first
original.label: Gordy
original.released: Issued as a 7-inch single on Gordy (Motown) on 9 May 1972, backed with “Friendship Train”; produced by Norman Whitfield. It did not reach an album until the group’s Law of the Land in 1973.
original.charted: No. 63 on the US pop chart and No. 24 R&B — a modest showing that Whitfield evidently judged a miss.
original.cover: The Temptations, released 28 September 1972 on Gordy from the album All Directions: No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, No. 5 R&B, three Grammy Awards in 1973 and a Grammy Hall of Fame induction in 1999.
trail: The song’s Wikipedia article ↗ gives The Undisputed Truth’s single as 9 May 1972 on Gordy at No. 63 pop / No. 24 R&B, and The Temptations’ as 28 September 1972 on the same label at No. 1.
The Undisputed Truth ↗ were assembled by Norman Whitfield in 1970 and repeatedly recorded songs he had written with The Temptations in mind — this was not the first time the two acts shared material.
The 1973 Gordy album Law of the Land ↗ carries the group’s recording as track two, 3:28, credited to Whitfield and Strong.

authors.name: The Undisputed Truth
authors.heading: The Undisputed Truth
authors.bio: Norman Whitfield assembled The Undisputed Truth in 1970 — Joe “Pep” Harris on lead with Billie Rae Calvin and Brenda Joyce Evans — explicitly as a laboratory for his psychedelic soul production ideas. Their one big hit was “Smiling Faces Sometimes” in 1971, itself a song Whitfield had first cut with The Temptations. The traffic ran both ways: they got “Papa Was a Rollin’ Stone” first, in a tight three-and-a-half-minute reading, and watched it be taken back. They followed Whitfield off Motown to his own label in 1975 and broke up in the early 1980s.

authors.name: The Temptations
authors.heading: The Temptations
authors.bio: The Temptations’ version, released on 28 September 1972 and carried on the album All Directions, is the reason anyone knows the song at all. It reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 5 R&B, took three Grammys in 1973, and entered the Grammy Hall of Fame in 1999. Nothing about that is undeserved — the long album mix, with the Funk Brothers stretching out before a word is sung, is one of the great records of the decade. The only error in the popular account is chronological: they were second, not first.

authors.name: Norman Whitfield and Barrett Strong
authors.heading: Norman Whitfield & Barrett Strong
authors.bio: Whitfield and Strong wrote “I Heard It Through the Grapevine”, “War”, “Just My Imagination” and this. Whitfield also produced both 1972 recordings, which is what makes the sequence unusual: the same producer, the same label and the same song, cut twice in one year with two different acts. Their Grammy for Best R&B Song in 1973 went to the writers, not the singers. Both were inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2004.

misattribution.heading: The fact-check
misattribution.intro: The song is nearly always filed as a Temptations original. It is a Temptations cover of a record that had already been released on their own label earlier the same year.

items.who: The Temptations originated “Papa Was a Rollin’ Stone” in 1972.
items.why: Their version went to No. 1 on the Hot 100, won three Grammys in 1973 and entered the Grammy Hall of Fame in 1999. It is the only version most listeners have heard.

items.who: The Undisputed Truth, single released 9 May 1972 on Gordy.
items.why: Backed with “Friendship Train”, it reached No. 63 on the pop chart and No. 24 R&B, and was later collected on the group’s 1973 Gordy album Law of the Land.
Whitfield produced both 1972 recordings. The 1973 Grammy for Best R&B Song went to the two of them as writers, not to either group.

misattribution.truthLine: First recorded by The Undisputed Truth, released 9 May 1972 on Gordy. The Temptations’ version followed on 28 September 1972.

context.heading: Why the second version buried the first
lead: The unusual thing here is that nobody was competing. Same song, same writer-producer, same record label, same year — Norman Whitfield simply decided the first attempt had not got there and did it again. The Undisputed Truth’s reading runs about three and a half minutes and behaves like a single. Whitfield’s re-cut with The Temptations abandoned that discipline entirely, opening with minutes of Funk Brothers vamp before a vocal arrives, and it is that patience — the sheer nerve of making a hit record wait — that people remember.

There is also the matter of who was singing. The Undisputed Truth were a Whitfield studio project with one hit behind them; The Temptations were The Temptations, with four lead voices to trade the verses between. The chart record tells the rest: No. 63 pop for the original, No. 1 for the cover, and a Grammy Hall of Fame induction in 1999 for the version that came second.
detailsBody: Written by Norman Whitfield and Barrett Strong; Whitfield produced every version discussed here.
9 May 1972 — The Undisputed Truth release “Papa Was a Rollin’ Stone” as a single on Gordy, backed with “Friendship Train”. It reaches No. 63 pop and No. 24 R&B.
28 September 1972 — Whitfield’s re-recording with The Temptations is issued on Gordy, drawn from the album All Directions. It reaches No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 5 R&B.
1973 — The Temptations’ record wins three Grammys, including Best R&B Song for Whitfield and Strong as writers.
1973 — The Undisputed Truth’s recording finally appears on an album, Law of the Land (Gordy), by which point the song belongs to somebody else.
context.pull: Whitfield did not lose the song to a rival. He took it back from himself.
